title: Chicken Parm with Spaghetti
subtitle: crunchy Parmesan-breaded cutlets under marinara and bubbly mozzarella
imageAlt: Breaded chicken Parmesan with melted mozzarella next to spaghetti in marinara
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Boneless skinless chicken breasts, 2 large (~800 g)

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen breasts? Thaw them in the fridge overnight (about 24 h).
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a sheet pan with parchment.
Put a big pot of salted water on to boil now for the spaghetti.
Pick a plain or traditional marinara (no visible basil leaves) — Classico Traditional or No Name both work.

items.name: boneless skinless chicken breasts
items.note: 2 large, sliced in half into 4 thin cutlets

steps.title: Make even cutlets
steps.text: Slice each breast in half horizontally, then pound to an even 1–1.5 cm thickness between plastic wrap. Even thickness = juicy and cooked through at the same time. Pat dry and season with salt, pepper and garlic powder.

steps.title: Set up the breading
steps.text: Three shallow dishes: flour; beaten eggs; panko mixed with ½ cup Parmesan, Italian seasoning and garlic powder. Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then press firmly into the crumbs on both sides.

steps.title: Pan-fry until golden
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Fry 2 cutlets at a time, 3 minutes per side, until deep golden (they finish in the oven). Move to the lined sheet pan.

steps.title: Sauce, cheese, bake
steps.text: Spoon about ¼ cup marinara on the centre of each cutlet (leave the edges crunchy), top with mozzarella and a sprinkle of Parmesan. Bake at 220°C (425°F) 12–15 minutes until the cheese bubbles and the chicken reads 74°C (165°F).

steps.title: Cook the spaghetti
steps.text: While it bakes, cook the spaghetti until al dente (box time, usually 9–10 min). Save ½ cup pasta water, drain, and toss with the warm marinara, butter and a splash of pasta water.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Let the chicken rest 3 minutes so the cheese sets, then serve on the spaghetti with extra Parmesan.

fixIt.fix: Pat the chicken dry before flouring, shake off extra flour, and press the crumbs on firmly. Don't move the cutlets in the pan until the first side is golden.
The oil was too hot or the cutlets too thick. Pound thinner; the oven finishes the cooking — always check for 74°C (165°F).
Bake on a wire rack set in the sheet pan, and keep the sauce on the centre only.
Season every layer — salt on the chicken and garlic/Italian seasoning in the crumbs. A pinch of salt in the marinara helps too.

saleTip: Classico and No Name pasta sauce often go 2 for $5 at No Frills, and shredded mozzarella (320 g) hits about $5–6 on sale. Buy chicken breast club packs on flyer weeks (~$9–10/kg).
swap: Use chicken thighs pounded thin, or make it with pork cutlets (cook to 71°C / 160°F).
leftovers: Fridge 3 days. Reheat cutlets in the air fryer at 175°C (350°F) 5–6 min (or oven 190°C / 375°F, 10 min) so they stay crisp; spaghetti microwaves fine.
source: Based on tested chicken Parmesan methods (America's Test Kitchen, Preppy Kitchen): breaded cutlets, pan-fried then baked at 425°F.
prepAhead: Pound and bread the cutlets up to 1 day ahead; keep on a plate in the fridge, uncovered, so the crumbs stay dry.
Breaded cutlets can be frozen raw on a tray, then bagged (2 months) — fry from frozen 1–2 min longer per side, then bake to 74°C (165°F).
reheat: Air fryer 175°C (350°F) 5–6 min or oven 190°C (375°F) 10 min so the crust stays crisp. Spaghetti: microwave with a splash of water. Reheat to 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Simple breaded cutlets with jarred sauce and mozzarella over spaghetti.

stepNotes.1: Basic: plain panko with the flour and egg — season the cutlets well instead.
stepNotes.4: Basic: toss the pasta with the warm sauce, no butter.

fancy.note: Fresh-style mozzarella, Parmesan crust, a garlic butter spaghetti and a crisp golden edge.

stepNotes.4: Fancy: melt the extra butter with the garlic 1 minute before tossing in the pasta and sauce.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Twirl the spaghetti into a nest with tongs, lean the cutlet against it, and finish with Parmesan and a crack of black pepper.

plating: Twirl the spaghetti into a tall nest with tongs in a ladle.
Lean the cutlet against the nest, crispy edge up.

why.1-0: Flour lets the egg stick so the crumb doesn't slide off.
why.1-3: Parmesan in the crumb adds savoury flavour and browns beautifully.
why.1-6: Enough oil fries the crumb golden; too little and it goes patchy.

funFact: Chicken parm is an Italian-American creation. Its ancestor, parmigiana from southern Italy, is made with fried eggplant, not chicken.
